organizations.description: Mobility behavior platform powering operator apps: journey detection, BIBO ticketing (built the MTA app)

paragraphs: Axon Vibe sells a smartphone-based, multi-modal mobility platform to public transport operators and authorities. The idea is to match a rider's predicted travel patterns against real-time traffic on roads and rail, then offer more efficient and less polluting travel options.

Patented location tracking predicts what people are going to do next, and psychological communication interventions are used to shift their behaviour. Riders who respond are rewarded with travel fare incentives financed by green governmental funds, plus rewards provided by local merchants. The platform is also sold to enable automatic ticketing, incentivise behaviour change and optimise customer flow management. For cities, understanding why and how people travel in real time is presented as the basis for more accurate planning.

Door-to-door journey detection powers Deutsche Bahn check-in and be-out ticketing, for example in Greater Nuremberg. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority launched its official MTA app in March 2024. Founded in 2014, the company describes a team of more than 100 software engineers, data scientists, location analytics experts, psychologists and communication specialists. Its predecessor Endoxon delivered core technology for Google Maps and was acquired by Google in 2006.

quote.text: Inspire people to change their travel habits

organizations.name: BusPas
organizations.description: Solar smart bus stops with edge AI plus the ORA platform: signage, lane enforcement, passenger counting

paragraphs: BusPas upgrades, connects and modernizes urban furniture, starting with bus stops. It equips that furniture with sensors and edge computing meant to improve transit, protect user privacy and enhance security. The buyers are municipalities and transit agencies looking to optimize operations and improve services.

The ORA Ecosystem is the platform side, giving public transit agencies, cities and their officials access to data services linked to infrastructure within their municipality. The stops display real-time bus wait times and occupancy, count waiting passengers, and track boarding and alighting to analyze connections and origins and destinations. The system can also send specific requests to control traffic lights for buses and emergency vehicles. SaferSmart Zones is a turnkey bus and transit lane enforcement offering. Solar panels are added to minimize dependence on the grid. The products are described as a modular ecosystem of solar-powered, AI-enabled street infrastructure for transit reliability, safety, enforcement and passenger experience.

The company says it started in 2017. It works through standing contracts, so new legislation or an RFP is not required. A statement on the site is attributed to the mayor of Sainte-Julie, Québec. A headline says its smart stop technology was deployed across the TTC network ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026.

quote.text: Every city needs a digital twin to test the efficacy and impact of programs and make data based decisions.

paragraphs: Spare sells operations software that a public transit agency runs its service on. The modes it covers include paratransit, microtransit and fixed route, along with asset management.

In one system an agency handles scheduling and dispatch, the rider experience, fleet health, and compliance and reporting. Because paratransit trips are often contracted out, the platform pulls trips from different providers into one place. Eligibility applications and rider records are digitized, which the company says speeds up the review process. On the fixed route side, an agency can plan service, publish a GTFS feed, build schedules and run live operations together. A voice assistant answers rider calls for bookings, arrival times and common questions.

The platform is described as built to meet ADA, NTD and grant reporting requirements. It connects through open APIs, GTFS, AVL feeds and single sign-on rather than replacing what a technology team already runs. Spare puts its reach at more than 230 communities. Its fixed route page describes coordinating a large event shuttle for LA Metro.

paragraphs: May Mobility develops autonomous driving technology and brings it to ride-hail platforms, cities, campuses and businesses. Its operations run from rural Minnesota to Atlanta and the dense streets of Japan.

The cornerstone of the technology is a system the company calls Multi-Policy Decision Making. It is described as a real-time, reinforcement-learning AI algorithm. Vehicles generate training examples relevant to their current environment and learn while driving. The sensor stack and the decision-making platform work together to monitor the road and run simulations of possible situations and hazards.

An autonomous ride-hail preview is live on Lyft. The site notes a first autonomous vehicle fleet deployed with Lyft in Atlanta. It also lists a strategic partnership with Uber to scale autonomous vehicles. An investment from Grab is tied to expansion into Southeast Asia. The chief executive is Edwin Olson.

organizations.name: Beep
organizations.description: Turnkey autonomous shuttle operations for transit agencies, airports, and communities

paragraphs: Beep plans, deploys and manages autonomous shuttles for private and public communities. The services answer demand for alternative modes of transportation within communities, campuses and municipalities. Routes run inside geo-fenced areas at a controlled speed.

Deployments are built around first and last-mile trips, linking retail to residential areas, remote parking to campus amenities, and underserved communities to transit stops and stations. The service portfolio runs from upfront analysis, planning and design through turnkey operation of an autonomous mobility network. Underneath sits AutonomOS, a vehicle-agnostic platform for multi-passenger autonomous mobility services. It plans service modes from fixed route to demand-responsive variants. In-cabin monitoring built on machine learning lets remote supervisors react to a passenger safety or roadway issue.

The platform is built for public transit operators and authorities. The company reports deployments in six states and two dozen deployments overall. The purpose-built shuttles carry ADA-compliant wheelchair ramps and restraints. One announced project, ATL Spoke, is a pilot with Atlanta Beltline that the company says is in service and open to the public.

quote.text: Beep delivers the next generation of shared mobility services utilizing driverless, multi-passenger vehicles.

organizations.name: Applied Information
organizations.description: Connected-vehicle ITS and the Glance smart-city platform: signal monitoring, preemption, school beacons

paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.

organizations.description: AI permitting and land-use copilot: research assistant, guided applications, staff permit center ($3.6M seed; Bellevue, Louisville Metro)

paragraphs: Govstream.ai sells permitting software to cities and counties, aimed at the point where an applicant is trying to work out what their project actually requires. It is positioned as an addition to the systems a city already runs rather than a replacement for them.

A research assistant answers questions about a specific property, using zoning, overlays and GIS data so an applicant can see what applies to that parcel. An application assistant takes the plans first, pulls project details out of them and prefills the forms. A completeness score flags gaps before anything is submitted. Staff get a console that holds permit data, adopted codes, GIS layers, historical permits and conversations in one searchable place.

The company names Bellevue, Washington, as the site of its first pilot and reports that it cut inbound questions. Louisville is described as building an end-to-end workflow meant to stop incomplete applications before they are submitted. Everett is listed as another partner city. The site describes the product as SOC 2-ready and able to work with a city's existing infrastructure. Its press section links coverage of a seed round.

organizations.name: Starbridge
organizations.description: AI public-sector GTM intelligence: buying signals from gov/school board meetings, budgets, RFPs - sold to vendors selling to gov

paragraphs: Starbridge sells an AI sales intelligence platform to companies whose customers are public-sector buyers. The target user is anyone selling into state and local government, K-12 districts, or higher education.

The platform collects buying signals from public sources such as district and university websites, board and trustee minutes, budget reports, grants, news, job postings, and FOIA requests. A signal, in the company's definition, is an early sign that a district, university, or agency is planning to spend. It claims to scan more than 320,000 public sector entities daily, surfacing budgets, board discussions, and leadership changes. Those signals and enriched accounts push into Salesforce and HubSpot. The platform also centralizes thousands of state, local, education, and university bid portals.

The buyers are go-to-market teams, and the company puts the number at more than 400 selling to government agencies, K-12, and higher education. On data quality, Starbridge cites a recent test of 14,000 emails with a 98% accuracy rate. New accounts are assigned a customer success manager who builds a tailored target list and syncs it into the CRM in the first week.

paragraphs: 8A Payments sells jails a way to take bail payments by card at the booking desk, so a person in custody can pay their own bail without cash. The company describes itself as a payments technology business built specifically for the cash bail market in the United States.

In the model it describes, the government entity rather than the vendor is the merchant of record. The site says the detainee pays an 8% service fee at checkout and the jail pays nothing. One deployment path ships a card reader straight to the booking desk with no software to install. The other integrates with a jail management system or biometric identification platform a facility already runs. The company states that it is CJIS compliant and PCI DSS certified.

The buyers named are sheriffs and jail administrators, and the same framework is said to cover court fees, fines and probation payments. A charter program offers a facility live access to the platform without a long term commitment. The company says it was founded and is headquartered in Georgia. It names Worldpay as its payment processing partner. David Forbes is listed as chief executive and majority shareholder, and co-founded the company with three other executives.

quote.text: 8A Payments LLC is a payments technology company purpose-built to serve the cash bail market in the United States.

organizations.name: ArcSuite AI
organizations.description: No-code AI government operations platform - exhibited at NIGP 2026

paragraphs: A-Frame Solutions sells ArcSuite AI, a no-code operations platform for federal, state, local and education agencies. Agencies use it to track work, evaluate vendors, compose documents and analyze data in one place, without developers.

Four integrated modules make up the suite, and a customer can use one or all four. ArcTracker holds configurable items, checklists, role-based access, relationships and rollups, and is the record every other module hangs off. ArcInsight is an assistant that answers plain English questions grounded in that tracker data. That assistant is powered by Claude on AWS Bedrock. ArcProcure covers solicitations, evaluations and contract management end to end, while ArcSelect is a multi-evaluator consensus platform for scoring or ranking decisions.

A-Frame Solutions was founded in 2014 by three former federal Contracting Officers. Its first contract was with the NOAA acquisition and grants office. The platform is available on GSA MAS Schedule 47QRAA18D003H. State agencies, counties, cities and special districts can buy it through the Purchasing Solutions Alliance cooperative with no competitive solicitation required. FedRAMP authorization is listed as in process. An IRS contract and an Authority to Operate brought ArcSuite AI into live federal production.

quote.text: Founded in 2014, A-Frame has been supporting federal agencies for over a decade.

Alongside payroll sits SmartCompliance, described as a connected operating system that unifies compliance work living outside or beside a customer's HCM system. Drivers start, stop, extend and pay for a session from an app. Operators run payment stations and in-car integrations from the same platform. License plate recognition can start and end sessions automatically as cars enter and leave. The company says its EV solutions connect with more than 400 charge point operators. For city planners, dashboards report parking use, traffic trends and mobility patterns to guide planning.

Arrive describes itself as a coming together of Flowbird Group, EasyPark Group, Parkopedia and others. The about page dates the story back to 1955. That timeline opens with Cale installing its first parking meters. Within the group, Flowbird is described as delivering mobility solutions in over 6,000 cities across 80 countries. EasyPark is described as present in over 4,000 cities across more than 20 countries.

paragraphs: Auror sells a retail crime intelligence platform to retailers and law enforcement agencies, built to bring crime intelligence together across a network of both. Retailers capture events in the platform, connect the dots between stores and cases, and identify potential threats.

Auror Core comprises five modules: Intel for incident reporting, Connect the Dots for AI-assisted person of interest matching with human verification, Investigate for case management, Insights for analytics and Audit for compliance workflows. Reported incidents build into in-depth profiles of the people and vehicles affecting an organization. Investigators then use that intel to build, collaborate on and resolve cases. A Risk Detection add-on extends this to prevention, with automatic alerts when known vehicles of interest enter a location. For law enforcement, the Retail Crime Hub, designed by Auror and Axon, moves packaged evidence from retailers straight into Axon Evidence for intake.

Auror puts its network at more than 85,000 stores and more than 3,500 law enforcement agencies, with a decade of accumulated intelligence across them. Auror says Cosentino's Food Stores achieved a 346% return on investment and a reduction of more than 90% in reporting time with the platform. The company has set itself the goal of reducing retail crime by 50% over the next five years.

quote.text: Unlike traditional case management tools, simplify incident reporting and enable secure collaboration between stores, retailers, and law enforcement, turning incidents into patterns, and patterns into outcomes.

paragraphs: CRIMEWATCH runs public-facing portals and a communications platform for police agencies. The platform is built for law enforcement and is described as CJIS-ready. Residents use it to find a local public safety portal, where agency updates and active warrants from across the network are posted.

The suite has four parts. A workflow product gives an agency one workspace to draft, route, approve and publish to web, mobile and social with a clear chain of command and audit history. Approval routing is configurable so an officer drafts, a supervisor reviews and a public information officer or command approves. A collaboration layer lets agencies, task forces and regional partners share intelligence and coordinate in real time. An AI assistant turns incident details into public messaging, with drafts still routed through review and approval.

The public side spans responsive portals, a unified national mobile app and TV kiosks, described as ADA compliant and multilingual. Information moves both ways, with anonymous tips linked to specific content, online reporting, camera and special-needs registries and vacation checks. The company says the community platform connects more than 360 agencies. Pricing is based on the population an agency serves.

quote.text: Solved cases start with a tip. Tips start with trust.

organizations.description: Purchasing card audit and compliance monitoring - exhibited at NIGP 2026

paragraphs: Card Integrity reviews the expense data of universities, corporations, and public institutions so that procurement and sourcing staff can catch policy problems and grow their card programs. The company presents itself as an extension of the client's procurement team, taking the expense review workload off internal staff.

Its main service covers all of an organization's spend data rather than a sample, looking for fraud, non-compliance, and savings opportunities. A companion service flags duplicate payments across accounts payable invoices and commercial card transactions. Another analyzes the receipts submitted through a client's spend portal and reports back when information is missing or incorrect. The company also builds online commercial card training courses tailored to each client's own policy. Rather than handing over a generic tool, it maintains an in-house system and pairs each client with a dedicated forensic principle.

The company observes that many businesses still relied on manual transaction reconciliation in 2008 and that many still do. Doug and Anita Hindsley expanded the early services across payment types and founded Card Integrity. It is headquartered in the Chicagoland area and serves clients in the United States and in more than 50 countries. Client programs range from 500 to five million company card transactions a month. The client base is described as including healthcare, higher education, government, infrastructure, military, and not-for-profit organizations.

A resident starts in their own words and the software asks follow-up questions, capturing people, places, property, evidence, legal elements and agency-required facts. The company states that it automatically detects and translates more than 100 languages in real time, so a resident can report in their native language. Report types cover theft, vehicle burglary, shoplifting, vandalism, fraud, forgery, harassment, threats and hit and run, and each department configures which ones to turn on. Anything describing an emergency or a crime in progress is pointed to 911 instead.

Finished records land in a review queue where department personnel correct and approve them before they move into the agency records system. The company lists Versaterm, Axon Records, Tyler Technologies, CentralSquare and Mark43 among the records platforms it pushes reports into. It says the product runs on CJIS-compliant infrastructure hosted on AWS GovCloud, with data encrypted at rest and in transit. Published department stories describe Laredo Police opening a smartphone-friendly reporting path for eligible incidents.

paragraphs: deleteme helps people find where their personal information is exposed online and works to have it removed. The company describes itself as a global privacy and digital exposure platform for individuals, families, professionals, executives, and businesses.

A free scan looks across data brokers, search engines, data breaches, the dark web, and other online sources. Signing up returns two complimentary reports showing where a person's information is currently exposed. After payment, staff process the request using both manual and automated methods, with status updates as each stage completes. Buyers can choose subscriptions for ongoing monitoring or one-time online reports for a single assessment. A companion service, CyberDeleteme, sells pay-as-you-go privacy intelligence, dark web monitoring, and cybersecurity scans.

The service was founded by Criton Tornaritis, described on the site as an accomplished attorney. The company states that it is not a data broker and does not maintain or commercially distribute databases of personal information. It also states that its reports must not be used for employment, credit, insurance, tenant screening, licensing, or other eligibility decisions. Its published case studies describe helping military officers reduce operational risk by removing exposed personal data from people-search and data broker sites.

organizations.description: Software for first responder agencies - exhibited at IACP 2026

paragraphs: GovWorx sells CommsCoach, an AI-powered software platform that emergency communications centers use to hire, train, evaluate and support 9-1-1 telecommunicators. It is aimed at the ECC leaders responsible for improving the performance of 9-1-1 professionals. Its modules follow a telecommunicator from candidate through career, linking HIRE, TRAIN, QA and ASSIST in one system, with PROMOTE added for choosing supervisors.

CommsCoach HIRE measures aptitude, resilience, accuracy and composure through structured testing and AI-supported scoring, with tests run onsite or remotely. QA automatically pulls every eligible call and radio transmission, matches transcripts to CAD event data and scores them against the agency's own policies. During live calls, ASSIST listens, transcribes and prompts the call-taker with the policy-specific questions the situation requires. PROMOTE is an evidence-based assessment that identifies leadership potential in supervisor candidates and pairs each result with a personalized development pathway.

An emergency communications administrator at the O'Fallon Police Department in Missouri is quoted saying call-taking compliance rose from single digits to 96% with ASSIST, APCO guidecards and complete QA. In June 2026 APCO International and GovWorx announced a partnership to bring APCO's communications protocols into CommsCoach ASSIST. In August 2026 GovWorx added NEAL, an adaptive non-emergency call handling tool that escalates to a human telecommunicator whenever judgment is needed.

paragraphs: Kodex sells a portal for processing subpoenas and other legal data requests, built for the companies that receive them. Those buyers manage requests from law enforcement through one centralized platform that Kodex says protects both compliance obligations and user privacy. The platform verifies every agent, encrypts every exchange, and keeps a complete record of how each request happened, and the company says requests close in days instead of weeks when both sides work in one system.

Compliance requirements become automated intake forms that catch issues before they start, and a dashboard shows request status, deadlines, and team responses. A single workspace replaces scattered email threads, so a team can work on each request internally and with government agents. Transparency reports generate in seconds, which Kodex pitches as preparation for audits and questions from regulators. Kodex describes itself as the only data request portal used by more than 15,000 government agencies.

Kodex was founded in 2020 in Boston by former FBI counterterrorism agent Matt Donahue. The company says its verification systems stop thousands of fake law enforcement requests, protecting the integrity of legitimate ones. A Coinbase vice president is quoted calling Kodex a partner when engaging with regulators. Bitget's chief compliance officer is also quoted. The feature list ends with SOC2, GDPR, and PCI compliance.

quote.text: Kodex moves critical data exchanges from faxes and emails to a verified, encrypted platform that keeps bad actors away from our data, and off the streets

competitors.why: AI investigative intelligence over case evidence and jail calls with CJIS-compliant AI chat, sold to the same detective bureau.
AI fusing video, phone extractions and jail calls into case timelines for the same investigator buyer weighing an AI investigations tool.

paragraphs: Longeye sells an AI-powered investigative workspace that law enforcement agencies use to analyze digital evidence. An investigator uploads video, audio, phone extractions, social media exports, financial records, and images, then asks questions in plain language. Every answer links back to the exact moment in a video, recording, message, or image, so a finding can be checked later.

Audio and video are transcribed and translated, with searchable transcripts across Spanish, Mandarin, and 99+ more. Each call then lands on a timeline color-coded by relevancy so the conversations most likely to matter come first. A map view plots GPS tracker pings, Cellebrite extraction data, CDR lat/long, and ALPR hits, with a slider that animates movement over time. A standalone product, Longeye Monitor, applies the same engine to jail call review for corrections agencies and jail facilities.

Longeye says it is deployed across the country, from major metropolitan departments and state bureaus of investigation to corrections intelligence units running jail call analysis. Chief Darrell Lowe of the Redmond Police Department is quoted crediting it with closing gaps in a cold-case homicide. On security, the company states it is SOC 2 Type II certified, isolates evidence per agency on dedicated US infrastructure, and never uses evidence to train a large language model. Longeye has raised $5M in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz's American Dynamism Fund.

quote.text: The truth is buried in the evidence. Longeye finds it 100x faster.

paragraphs: MCM sells software that helps public safety agencies stay ahead of risk, increase safety and maintain compliance by managing assets, certifications, maintenance and inspections in one connected platform. The product is framed as intelligent operational readiness for public safety.

Asset tracking keeps a full lifecycle history from procurement through retirement. Issuance and chain of custody let staff issue serialized assets and consumable inventory in the same transaction. Work orders are created automatically when an inspection fails. Custom templates can be built for any inspection type, including vehicles, weapons, jump bags, respirators, facilities and sites. An open REST API is offered for connecting other systems, and the integrations page claims to be the only platform that integrates directly with major radio manufacturers.

The company cites 300+ public safety agencies nationwide. For fire agencies the aim is to keep apparatus, gear and crew inspection-ready at every station and before the next call comes in. For government and utilities it gives full asset visibility and tracks grant-funded resources. A news post announces Anthony Rotoli as new CEO. Agencies that would rather not administer the system themselves can buy managed services, pitched as maximum impact without the administrative overhead.

paragraphs: Nutanix sells infrastructure software that lets organizations build, manage and optimize IT across on-premises, edge and public cloud environments. At the core is a platform with hyperconverged compute, storage, virtualization and networking.

The storage layer consolidates file, object and block storage into one platform with integrated cyber security and ransomware protection. A database service automates provisioning, patching, cloning, backup and recovery, and supports Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and MongoDB. Day-to-day work happens in Prism, which monitors and manages VMs, storage and networks across on-premises clusters and public clouds from a single console. Prism is included with Nutanix Cloud Infrastructure at no additional cost. For larger estates, Nutanix Central is a cloud console for viewing and managing Nutanix services deployed on-premises or on Nutanix Cloud Clusters.

The home page counts more than 30,000 companies as customers. Public sector examples include the Indonesia Election Committee, which the company says improved legal response times by 90% across 210 million voter records. Another describes London Gatwick Airport scaling support to fifty million passengers. The company also reports being named a Leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant.

paragraphs: Pimloc sells Secure Redact, an automated system for the bulk redaction of personal data from video. It is aimed at private and public organizations that want to automate data privacy compliance while still getting operational value from their video. Customers use it to process video for data subject access requests and freedom of information requests.

The system's models recognize identifiers such as faces, heads and license plates the way a human observer would, then redact and classify them automatically. It can be applied selectively, removing some or all faces or all vehicle registration details, and it is trained to perform on low-definition CCTV footage. Pimloc states that Secure Redact detects and anonymizes over 99% of identifiable PII in security video. It also says redaction with its AI runs 200 times faster than doing the job by hand.

The company says its capabilities are deployed across transport, public safety, telehealth, insurance, retail, policing and local government. A second product, Pholio, classifies visual content, and Pimloc has used it to evaluate automated detection of online harms. Founders Simon Randall, the CEO, and James Leigh, the CTO, co-created the Autographer wearable image capture device at a previous business, and the privacy challenges of always-on capture led them to start Pimloc.

quote.text: Automated anonymization is the only way to keep up with changing privacy legislation and to responsibly unlock the value of aggregated video data for business operations.

paragraphs: SAP Concur sells software for handling business expenses, travel and supplier invoices. The pitch is a single platform that gives a company better visibility and control over spending. The company says the products are designed for businesses of all sizes.

Concur Expense is cloud-based expense management software covering the stretch from submitting a receipt to being reimbursed. Key details are pulled from receipts and card transactions automatically, so staff key in less data by hand. Submitted expenses are checked against company rules before they move any further along. A companion product handles the step before money is spent, automating requests and approvals against travel and expense policy. A separate audit product applies machine learning to fraud and compliance risks both before and after reimbursement.

The platform is meant to sit on top of systems a customer already runs, with hundreds of pre-built connectors and open APIs for anything custom. The company says its models are trained on one of the largest expense datasets in the industry and improve as more transactions pass through. Expense pricing is published in US dollars and varies with monthly commitment. The top tier is set aside for businesses that need the most advanced capabilities.

paragraphs: Tanium sells software that gives IT and security teams continuous visibility across an entire endpoint estate. A single agent covers real-time threat hunting, autonomous detection and response, and deep forensics. Vulnerability monitoring runs continuously with risk scoring based on actual exploitability rather than CVSS alone.

A layer called Atlas sits on top, unifying investigation and remediation with agentic AI over real-time endpoint intelligence. Operators type questions in plain English and Atlas translates them into live endpoint queries. Actions then execute within autonomy limits the operator defines. Native connectors link the platform to ServiceNow, Microsoft and Splunk.

Customer pages describe Best Buy consolidating data into a single pane of glass. Another describes Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust keeping thousands of endpoints patched and up to date. That page says the platform gives full visibility into all 3,000 PCs and servers. The homepage says the company was named a Leader and positioned furthest in Completeness of Vision in a 2026 Gartner report.

brands.name: NextRec (formerly PerfectMind)
brands.description:
PerfectMind is the former name of the product now sold as nextRec, and nextrec.com keeps a page for it that opens "PerfectMind Software is now nextRec". That page defines the product as "a frictionless, all-in-one recreation management software designed for government agencies and private recreation facilities", and says PerfectMind "serves parks and recreation organizations, martial arts studios, higher-education recreation centers, swim schools, homeowner associations, and facilities offering classes and camps to their community members". The government function is the registration-and-facilities back office of a parks and recreation department: online and on-site registration for "courses, private lessons, drop ins", an "intelligent conflict manager" for scheduling community events, one-time and recurring facility rentals with customizable contract templates and digital customer signatures, point of sale for memberships and passes, built-in email marketing so departments do not sync to outside software, and real-time reporting across "any object or table in your database". A Citywide POS module is offered to consolidate payments across a municipality. The brand still has live surfaces: the knowledge base and user community on nextrec.com both sit at community.perfectmind.com, and the PCI DSS certificate the site links to is filed as "PerfectMind PCI DSS Certificate".

The page gives the family history plainly. "PerfectMind was founded in 1998." "PerfectMind's software was acquired by Xplor Technologies in 2020. In 2022, PerfectMind rebranded to become nextRec." On what changed: "The PerfectMind software platform remains built and powered by the same team - aside from changing its name to nextRec the only change is that PerfectMind software is now part of a global ecosystem with powerful backing, integrations, and support." That answers the "why does this one exist" question differently from its siblings: PerfectMind is not a separate product sitting beside nextRec, it is the same product under its previous name, kept addressable because agencies bought it under that name. The same page says "Xplor Technologies is the parent company of PerfectMind" and that Xplor "serves over 140 markets globally, 75,000 customers daily, and employs over 2,000 Xplorers across the globe". One conflict is worth recording rather than resolving: nextrec.com says PerfectMind was founded in 1998, while Xplor's corporate site says "Founded in 1988, NextRec". Both are the family's own materials and they disagree; neither was treated as settled here.

brands.name: ePACT
brands.description:
ePACT Network sells emergency and health forms automation, described on its homepage as "Emergency and health forms automation that integrates seamlessly with rec management systems" and on its parks and recreation page as a way for "rec leaders to collect, manage and access health & emergency information, waivers and consent forms - all in one secure, compliant platform". The government function is narrow and specific: it is the participant-paperwork layer under a parks and recreation department's programs. The site lists what it collects - "emergency forms with contact information and instructions, medical forms, waivers, consent forms, and personal health and safety needs", plus immunization records, medication authorization forms, allergies, dietary restrictions, medical history and signed consent forms. Named capabilities are configurable eForms, online and offline access, multi-channel communications, search, filtering and reporting, API integration, and paperless check-in and check-out with a "tailorable contact pick up list" for who may collect a child. Buyers named on the site are parks and recreation departments, YMCAs, camps and JCCs, schools, and sports associations. Public-sector customers quoted by name include the City of Kettering, OH, the San Francisco Recreation & Park Department, CA, the City of Newton Parks & Recreation, MA, the Town of Cary, NC, and the Deerfield Park District, IL. On compliance the site claims SOC II Type 2, HIPAA in the US, and PIPA, PIPEDA and FOIPPA in Canada, hosted on Microsoft Azure. Families use it free, storing a "Private Personal Emergency Record (PPER)".

ePACT sits differently in the family from the other brands: it is not a system of record for registration, it is the forms layer that attaches to one. Its own site says it integrates "with your existing registration system, like ActiveNet, Daxko, RecTrac (and more!)" - RecTrac being the sibling Vermont Systems product, ActiveNet and Daxko being competitors of the family. That is the answer to why it exists alongside three registration platforms: it is sold across all of them, including rivals. Its distribution runs through associations rather than the Xplor brand - it is "Exclusive Partner of the NRPA" with member discounts, a "Preferred vendor of the YMCA of the USA", and an "Emergency-supplies partner with the Canadian Red Cross". The family tie is real but quiet: the site footer reads "2026 ePACT Network | All Rights Reserved", with no Xplor copyright, yet it carries an Xplor Recreation logo image linking to cehrecreation.com, and ePACT is not one of the four brands listed on Xplor's own Xplor Recreation page. Its origin is on its about page: ePACT was inspired by a friend, Ayumi, separated from her two daughters during the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, and unable to learn they were safe for a full day.

brands.name: RecDesk
brands.description:
recdesk.com could not be read. Both the apex and www forms answer a plain fetch with an HTTP 202 and a Sucuri interstitial, and a real browser is served a "Robot Challenge Screen" that did not clear on repeated attempts. No attempt was made to defeat it, so nothing below comes from RecDesk's own site. What follows is from Xplor's corporate site, which is the family's own material. Xplor writes: "Founded in 2005, RecDesk provides scalable, easy-to-use software for parks and recreation departments, aquatic centers, schools, community centers, HOAs, and small municipalities. Its integrations with access control, GIS/address databases, and financial systems help teams streamline facility scheduling, program management, and operational workflows - reducing manual effort and system fragmentation." Xplor adds that "Business and community leaders can run more efficient programs, offer better resident experiences, and make data-driven decisions that strengthen their community services."

RecDesk is one of the four brands Xplor lists on its Xplor Recreation page, alongside Vermont Systems, NextRec and CampBrain, and Xplor's "Visit RecDesk" link points to recdesk.com. The distinction Xplor's own wording draws between the siblings is the size and type of buyer: RecDesk is described for "small municipalities", aquatic centers and HOAs, where Vermont Systems is described for "municipal, county, state, and federal military recreation organizations". RecDesk's postings run through the Rippling board shared across this family, clubessential-holdings-cjb, which also carries an asset named Xplor_Logo_withTag_Color.png. Beyond that, this record is deliberately short. Anything further about RecDesk's product, customers or scale would have to be invented, because its site refused to be read.

Xplor's corporate site says: "Founded in 1985, Vermont Systems is a leading recreation management platform built for municipal, county, state, and federal military recreation organizations. Its comprehensive operational, payment, and experience-management features help teams simplify daily tasks, modernize processes, and reduce manual work." ePACT, a sibling brand, describes it twice on its own site: "We have partnered with Vermont Systems, a market leader in recreation management software for parks & recreation, schools, and governments", and, using the company's initials, "We integrate with VSI, a market leader in recreation management software for parks & recreation, schools, and governments." ePACT also names the flagship product, listing RecTrac beside ActiveNet and Daxko as the registration systems it plugs into.

organizations.description: Satellite earth-observation imagery and change-detection analytics for agencies, insurance, and ag - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: EarthDaily is a geospatial company selling satellite imagery and analytics to governments and enterprises whose work depends on the physical world. Its stated purpose is daily monitoring of the earth's surface for broad area change detection.

Raw satellite data is captured through a purpose-built constellation and ground system. That data is then processed, calibrated and quality-controlled into scientifically accurate image products. One product, AiRD, is analysis-ready observation data engineered from the start for machine learning. Its spectral bands are calibrated to match Sentinel-2 and Landsat specifications. A second product, Maritime, is tuned for fast processing and detection of anomalies at sea.

The company focuses its products on agriculture, financial services, infrastructure, forestry and governments. Security organizations, analytics providers and coastal agencies are the named audience for the maritime data. A company timeline states that it was created in partnership with Antarctica Capital. The same timeline lists an acquisition of Descartes Labs and funding from Trinity Capital. It also records more than 500 agreements signed. A news item states the company achieved CEOS Analysis Ready Data compliance.

paragraphs: A-ICE provides IT solutions and integrated applications for airport operations, serving airports, airlines and ground handlers. The company says it has supplied airports, airlines, ground handlers and the military with software and IT for over 25 years. Its product range is grouped by customer type, covering airlines, airports, ground handlers and cargo.

The flight information display system shows timetables, gate and baggage belt information. It connects to the central database, A-ODB, and is built to run with minimal manual entry. A contract and billing product takes on the recording and billing of aeronautical fees, which the site calls a complex task for airports. The baggage reconciliation system, A-BRS, tracks bag location within the airport, at the gate and on the plane. A-MDS carries message exchange between applications, the A-ODB and airport sub-systems.

The head office is in Italy. The company states that it has provided consultation and installation across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. It says solutions are offered in the customer's region, language and currency, complying with local and international regulation. The site puts its experience in the field at over 25 years.

organizations.description: Mobile augmented-reality game platform licensed to airports, parks and public agencies to engage visitors with location-triggered educational missions and wayfinding-style content.

paragraphs: Agents of Discovery turns physical spaces such as museums, airports, campuses, libraries, stadiums and entire cities into interactive learning environments by blending AI-driven content generation with place-based augmented reality gameplay. Customers become what the company calls Mission Makers, turning their own stories, spaces and content into augmented reality experiences.

Location-based challenges are placed on site and tied to the customer's own content, or played from anywhere. A site can also deploy a fully customized AI avatar as its on-site guide. Self-guided tours are offered around the clock. Exhibits can be built for aquariums, zoos and museums. Text-to-speech and multiple language options are meant to keep the platform reachable for players with diverse abilities and backgrounds.

Airports are one named setting, where the pitch is turning downtime into interactive adventures built for travelers. Junior Ranger Missions on the platform cover subjects from palaeontology and fossils to International Migratory Bird Day. The chief academic officer works with public and private organizations across the United States, Australia and Canada on visitor experience. The company describes itself as a Harvard-incubated AI and augmented reality company.

organizations.description: Cloud identity management system (IDMS) purpose-built for US airport badge offices: applications, renewals, TSA audit compliance, training and scheduling, integrated with fingerprint, PACS (LenelS2) and training platforms.

paragraphs: AirBadge sells identity management software to airports in the United States, aimed at the badge office that issues and renews credentials. The company says it puts all of its resources into aviation so the software fits airport operations and TSA regulations. The product is described as built for 1542 and part 139 airports.

Applicants and badge holders enter their own details into the system. Those details are then sent directly to integrated systems, which removes a round of rekeying. It automates badge applications, appointment scheduling, training and testing, and cuts manual entry at fingerprinting, physical access control and TSC. Authorized signatories use it to invite new hires to apply and to authorize or block renewals. It runs on fully managed cloud infrastructure.

The site says more than 50 airports in the United States use it. It presents itself as a fit for airports of any size. The company announced LenelS2 factory certification and membership in the LenelS2 OpenAccess Alliance Program. Its software interfaces with the LenelS2 OnGuard access control system. Deployment is pitched in weeks rather than years.

quote.text: Built exclusively for 1542 and part 139 airports

organizations.name: Alcatraz
organizations.description: Alcatraz AI Rock: 3D facial authentication and tailgating detection device that replaces or augments badge readers at secure doors, integrating with existing access control systems.

paragraphs: Alcatraz makes facial authentication products that work with the badge readers and access control systems an organization already runs. The device, called Rock X, sits in line between the badge reader and the access control panel over Wiegand or OSDP.

Employees enroll at a station, remotely from a browser or phone, or automatically after repeated badge swipes at a door fitted with the device. Authentication happens on the device itself, and the company states that no sensitive data is stored or transmitted. Profiles are anonymized and tied to the badge ID already held in the customer's access control system. The same unit can act as a passive second factor, so a person badges in as usual and the face confirms the match. In lobbies it can be built directly into certain turnstiles. The management platform runs on premise or in the cloud.

Airports are one setting the company writes about, pairing face recognition with badges or PINs to add a second factor at restricted doors. One unnamed case summary on the site describes a global enterprise that put the device on turnstiles for more than 150,000 employees. The company says its approach helps customers conform with privacy regulations such as BIPA, CCPA and GDPR.

quote.text: authentication happens at the edge ensuring no sensitive data is stored or transmitted

It is the brand of FAAC Technologies dedicated to the parking and mobility industries. Its customers are operators running anything from single facilities to global networks.

The JUPITER product range covers the lane itself, with multiple combinations of entry and exit functions. Cabinets use full stainless steel construction. Jupiter is built to adapt to systems using license plate recognition, contract parking, credit card in and out parking, or online pre-paid parking. The range also includes automated pay stations, among them a cashless model. On the software side, JMS brings a parking operation into one cloud-based management system. Tools named J4Pay, J4M and J4H extend the operation beyond the lane.

The company dates its parking work to 1965. It calls itself one of the largest parking system manufacturers worldwide. Buyers are supported by direct sales representatives or value added resellers. The site sorts its offerings by sector on the premise that wherever a customer operates, there is a matching solution.

organizations.description: HEXWAVE walk-through concealed weapons detection plus body and shoe scanners for aviation checkpoints and public venues.

paragraphs: Liberty Defense makes AI-based detection equipment for finding concealed weapons and other threats in urban security and aviation settings. Its main product, HEXWAVE, is a walkthrough portal that screens for nonmetallic and metallic threats without asking people to remove shoes, jewelry, belts or jackets.

It uses active millimeter wave, video-rate 3D imaging and AI to detect concealed metallic and non-metallic weapons and other prohibited items. The company says the imaging captures over 400,000 voxels. No images are stored, and none are accessible by the security operator. The operator sees only a go or no-go screen with a clear alert. For aviation, Liberty holds exclusive licenses to two solutions developed by PNNL and funded by the Department of Homeland Security.

The home page states that Liberty delivers HEXWAVE to the TSA. It also says the company is developing screening for aviation workers. Named settings include hotels, schools, airports, public transit systems, places of religion and entertainment venues. On its finances, the company reports completing an initial public offering in the United States that raised approximately $20 million in gross proceeds.

quote.text: The system is non-intrusive, protecting the privacy and modesty of those being scanned while offering an unprecedented level of security

organizations.location: Paris, France (offices in San Francisco and Singapore)
organizations.description: LiDAR-based spatial intelligence software turning 3D sensor data into anonymous passenger flow, queue wait time and occupancy analytics for terminals and curbside.

paragraphs: Outsight sells software that turns 3D sensor feeds into a running account of how people, vehicles, and robots move through a site. The buyers are operators of large shared spaces such as airports, hospitals, and factories.

Anything entering the scene is given an anonymous identifier and held to centimeter precision until it leaves. No faces or plates are captured, only the geometry of motion. Operators define zones and the measures they care about, such as counting, density, queue length, wait time and throughput, and the analytics engine computes them continuously. Results come back as live 3D playback, custom indicators, alerts, dashboards, and APIs. Before any of that, a multi-vendor simulator tests layouts and sensor mixes and proposes the hardware configuration.

The company says the platform is deployed at scale across five continents. It calls the result a Motional Digital Twin and says these are running in production. Its newsroom announces a strategic partnership with AWS around spatial AI in aviation. The pitch behind all of it is that movement is the next layer of business to be digitized.

quote.text: The bottleneck of Physical AI is not models, it is real-world data

paragraphs: The Weather Company sells weather data, forecasting, and insights to consumers and businesses alike. The industries it names are advertising, aviation, media, and government.

Much of the business runs through a weather data API that customers fold into their own applications, business processes, or custom models. For aviation the pitch is converting complex meteorological data into decision-ready flight and ground insights. The stated aim there is fewer costly delays, better fuel use, and safer crews and passengers from preflight to touchdown. A separate government and defense line is aimed at mission risk from command centers to the tactical edge.

The company traces its work back nearly five decades, combining human meteorological expertise with technology. It also powers a portfolio of three consumer brands used daily around the world. Case studies describe Breeze Airways using its Fusion flight tracking to run more efficiently through major weather events and resume operations faster after disruptions. Another describes NASCAR unifying its weather intelligence with the company to make scheduling and safety calls.

paragraphs: AirWorks turns raw field data into mapping deliverables that engineering teams can work from. Its customers are teams in the telecom, power and civil sectors.

For new construction the company supplies the site data engineers use to plan, design and deliver builds. On the maintenance side the same outputs are used to find vegetation risks near infrastructure and keep assets compliant. Operators also use the data to decide where to send field crews.

paragraphs: CivicEye sells cloud software for law enforcement and prosecutors, pitched as a way to improve daily workflows and community outcomes. The platform has three main products: a records management system for police called CivicRMS, prosecutor case management called CivicCase, and judicial document management called CivicDocs. A fourth, CivicCase for Courts, is aimed at judges and clerks in municipal courts.

CivicRMS creates NIBRS-compliant reports from incident reports, and its validation tools track errors and point to fixes. Integrations with dispatch and jail systems let officers pull dispatch calls, incident details, arrest records and inmate data without leaving the RMS. CivicDocs holds digital evidence and generates audit logs that track the chain of custody between the arresting agency and the prosecutor's office. Users reach the system through role-based portals for prosecutors, clerks, law enforcement and defense attorneys.

The company traces its start to 2007, when it built software for police departments in upstate New York under the name J2 Software and later Agisent Technologies. It is now based in Charlotte, North Carolina, and says it has deployed its software to over 95 public safety and criminal justice agencies across the country. It also says its prosecutor software is used across Tennessee, where the entire Tennessee District Attorney General's Conference adopted it.

quote.text: Combining a modern cloud infrastructure with field-tested insights from across the U.S., CivicEye is changing the face of criminal justice and public safety software.

paragraphs: BriefCam sells video analytics software that makes recorded surveillance video searchable, actionable and quantifiable. Its patented VIDEO SYNOPSIS technology condenses hours of surveillance into a short summary by overlaying multiple events, each tagged with its original timestamp, onto a single frame that users can filter by object type and attributes. The software is camera-agnostic, integrates with video management systems such as XProtect, and also works as a standalone solution for agencies that only need file-based review.

Three modules, Review, Respond and Research, are used respectively for post-incident search, real-time alerts and quantifying data trends. Every customer needs Review as a base and can then add Respond, Research or both. License plate recognition works on any camera, with no need for dedicated LPR licenses per camera. For commercial users, people counting tracks queues and crowd movement and measures occupancy to improve space use and traffic flow.

BriefCam serves law enforcement, transportation, retail and more, across public and private sectors. Customer stories on the site cover Tlaxcala, Mexico, Villa El Salvador and the City of Hartford's real-time crime center. The site is published by Milestone Systems, which lists BriefCam among its products alongside the XProtect video management software.

An Evidencentral Marketplace of technology vendors is designed to make it simpler and faster for emergency communications, law enforcement and criminal justice agencies to bring evidence together.

paragraphs: Miller Mendel, Inc. creates, sells and supports software for city, county, state and federal public safety agencies. Its first and flagship product, eSOPH, is a cloud-based system for public agencies that must run in-depth pre-employment background investigations on their applicants. Since 2011 its customers have been city police departments, county sheriff's offices, state police agencies, district attorney's offices and other criminal justice entities.

The company says eSOPH has been credited with cutting the time to process a background investigation by more than 50%, so applicants can be hired more quickly. Partnerships with Experian and Fama Technologies add one-click retrieval of credit reports and of social media and online activity reports. A captain at the Riverside County Sheriff's Department in California, which conducts over 2,500 applicant investigations a year, estimates a 50% time saving per investigation.

Miller Mendel describes itself as a minority owned, small business. It reports serving over 16,000 agency users. More than 90% of new clients, it says, come by referral from existing eSOPH users. In April 2026 NEOGOV, a workforce management platform built for the public sector, announced it had acquired Miller Mendel and was bringing eSOPH into its public safety software portfolio. The release said eSOPH was used by more than 300 customers, including some of the largest law enforcement agencies in the country.

paragraphs: CalAmp sells telematics devices and cloud software that organizations use to monitor, track, and protect vehicles, equipment, and cargo. Its telematics cloud is pitched at fleet operators, logistics companies, equipment manufacturers, and the systems integrators who build on top of it.

Devices on the vehicle collect location, speed, engine health, driver behavior, and outside sensor readings in real time. The cloud then turns protocols such as CAN bus, J1939, OBD-II, and Modbus into clean, structured output. Customers pull that data through APIs, a cloud connector, or event-driven alerts. A device management layer lets administrators assign roles governing who can view, change, or execute particular management functions. Software can be prototyped, tested, and deployed to devices over the air.

CalAmp says the platform is built for commercial fleets and software providers in construction, trucking, utilities, the public sector, and equipment manufacturing. The company states it has been in business for 40 years, with thousands of customers and more than 275 approved or pending patents. paragraphs: Agile Fleet sells FleetCommander, a fleet management information system, to organizations that run vehicle fleets. Work orders capture hours, labor, parts and status. The company says it has partnered with municipalities, universities and commercial fleets. It also states that the platform is built on AWS GovCloud, aligned to NIST 800-53 and listed in the FedRAMP Marketplace.

paragraphs: CivicSmart sells cities a curb management system spanning smart hardware at the space, real-time intelligence on every event, enforcement, and the operations software that ties them together. It also aims at universities and campuses. Airports and transit hubs are another target, where rideshare zones, cell lots and passenger loading need managing.

Product lines run from single-space and multi-space meters with integrated sensor options. Curb sensors report real-time occupancy, plate capture, and evidence-grade detection. LaneMaster devices provide automated lane management for loading, pickup-dropoff, rideshare and commercial corridors. Officers write citations on AutoISSUE handhelds. PEMS unifies every meter, sensor, handheld and citation into one dashboard. It publishes open REST endpoints so cities can bring their own BI, GIS and analytics tools.

CivicSmart, Inc. describes itself as a Wisconsin company founded in 2015 around the idea of reimagining the curb. It says it acquired Duncan Parking Technologies from Duncan Solutions in 2015 and renamed it CivicSmart Parking Technologies. The site claims more than 1,500 cities and agencies served. It also claims more than 15 million parking meters shipped. The company says its team holds patents globally for vehicle-detection sensors and parking technologies.

paragraphs: PayByPhone sells a mobile app for paying for parking in a few taps, without coins or hunting for the machine. It is available in over 1,200 cities across North America and Europe, including universities and colleges.

A driver connects a credit or debit card to a PayByPhone account and pays from the phone. Where available, Google Pay or Apple Pay can complete the transaction instead. A session can be extended from the app, with no need to run back to the car to feed the meter.

The company dates its start to 2001 and a plan to take the pain out of parking. It now describes a mission spanning three continents. The home page puts all-time users at more than 125 million. Ownership sits with Lightyear Capital, a New York-based private equity firm with over US$8 billion in assets under management. The press page also announces a global partnership with SKIDATA covering parking and access control solutions. Jonny Combe is named as President and Chief Executive Officer.

paragraphs: Players Health sells insurance together with the staff and software a sports program needs to keep participants protected. The company dates the work to 2016 and has widened the roster since then to insurance, athlete safety, and employee benefits products and services. On the insurance side it describes athlete-first protection sold to youth sports nationwide.

Policies cover a league or program against unexpected accidents, injuries, or property damage. A separate directors and officers line is offered as legal protection for a board. Alongside the policies sits a suite of athlete safety products meant to protect youth and amateur athletes, fitness club members, and student athletes. Programs that do not know where to begin can ask for a Players Health Safety Score to work out what steps they need. Training is pitched at coaches and organizations building team cultures and keeping their programs positive and safe. paragraphs: SimpliGov sells a workflow platform for government agencies, built around the applications, approvals and casework that programs run on. Its stated scope is anything that moves through approvals, whatever the department.

Intake starts with online forms that meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Program teams lay out the steps on a drag-and-drop stage builder instead of writing custom code. The engine routes applications and decisions by rule, data threshold and the agency organizational structure. Approvals are signed inside the workflow with native e-signature tools. Dashboards track processing times, bottlenecks and audit trails.

Agency examples include New Castle County processing $322.8 million in emergency grants and passing its audit with zero findings. Another describes a California city automating more than 70 workflows and saving 17,000 labor hours a month. The forms page cites a federal accessibility mandate, 28 CFR Part 35, that larger public entities must meet by April 26, 2027. The platform is described as cloud-native and meeting government data privacy, security and accessibility mandates.

Alongside testing, the firm sells recruiting, human resource and investigative services.

A candidate completes one online application, takes one written exam and one physical ability test, fills out a single Personal History Statement, and has scores sent to one or many departments. Testing is continuous rather than annual, with hundreds of local testing opportunities each year across the United States. Agency programs also cover advertising and professional recruiting assistance, application intake processing, investigations, promotional testing and executive services. Candidates and departments see test scores in real time.

Hundreds of public safety agencies in the Pacific Northwest and beyond contract for pre-employment testing, investigative and promotional services. The site marks 25 years of the company. paragraphs: Black Mountain Software sells accounting, payroll, utility billing, and related software to small and medium-sized local governments throughout the United States. The company traces its founding to rural Montana.

Its fund accounting product carries general ledger, accounts payable, journal entries, cash bank reconciliation, and a wide range of compliant reports. Other applications handle permitting, licensing, and other community development work for local governments. Utility billing automates customer information management, meter-readings, and billing. A separate set of integrated applications covers a county's property tax needs. The software runs on the BMS Cloud, where updates arrive automatically as financial rules change.

The company says it is over 50 team members strong and provides 30 integrated applications purpose-built for municipalities, counties, special districts, and schools. It says it has become a valued partner to hundreds of clients. Its team members come from small towns and have worked in local governments as clerks and accountants. Published case studies include one on Ravalli County.

Its tax product, GenTax, is stated to be in use by more than sixty tax and revenue agencies worldwide. A driver and vehicle system covers licensing, identity services, titling, registration and permitting. Another product handles unemployment insurance and paid leave across tax, benefits and appeals. A child support system brings program management into a single place. Audit, collections and identity verification are offered alongside the software as services.

The buyers are national, state or provincial, and local government agencies. The company states its core software is in production at more than a hundred government agencies worldwide. It describes its own aim as being a provider of software and consulting services to government agencies.

paragraphs: Careers In Government runs a job board that connects candidates with roles in state and local government, education, and public service. Listings span titles from city managers and public health nurses to urban planners and environmental engineers.

Job seekers get free access to search postings, upload resumes, and reach public sector employers directly. Filters narrow results by location, salary, classification, or job type. Employers buy recruitment packages that include unlimited annual memberships, resume database access, and job postings. The company says those tools integrate with an agency applicant tracking system and support compliance.

The company dates its work in this market to 1996. It describes the platform as built by former public sector professionals. Visitors to the home page can sign up to have job alerts sent to their inbox.

paragraphs: The company sells election technology, and states its aim as delivering systems that are transparent, secure, accessible and reliable. Its site says the business was formed through the acquisition of Dominion Voting Systems and now trades as Liberty Vote. It describes itself as an American-owned nonpartisan election technology company.

The product range covers the election from ballot design through vote capture to results reporting. An election management system runs the whole election project from one database. Ballot marking devices come in configurations for in-person, accessible and early voting. Central count scanners handle absentee, vote-by-mail and precinct ballots. An audit record lets officials review ballot images alongside how the tabulator read each ballot. The systems work with verifiable paper ballots.

Customers are the jurisdictions it serves, and the company says older systems were retired so each one runs supported technology. In late 2025 it submitted a voting system called Frontier 1.0 to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission for certification under VVSG 2.0 standards. The company is owned by its founder and chairman, Scott Leiendecker.

quote.text: Liberty Vote Corporation is a new, 100% American-owned nonpartisan election technology company formed through the acquisition of Dominion Voting Systems.

organizations.name: Clear Ballot Group
organizations.description: Digital ballot scanning, tabulation and audit systems for election offices

paragraphs: Clear Ballot Group builds voting technology for the officials who run elections. The company started out doing post-election auditing. Its stated position is paper ballots that voters can review and verify.

The product line is grouped into tabulation, accessibility, election management, auditing, training and ballot printing. ClearCount, the central count system, runs with Fujitsu and ibml commercial scanners and can tabulate ballots created by all major voting systems. The newer Nexus hardware can be deployed either as a standalone tabulator or as a hybrid ballot marking device. Nexus does not rely on QR codes, barcodes or OCR to capture or count votes.

The company says its election technology is currently used in thirteen states. It reports partnerships with more than 150 jurisdictions. It also says its systems scale to jurisdictions of all sizes and respond to the budget realities of counties and municipalities.

quote.text: committed to paper ballots that voters can review, verify, and trust

organizations.description: Open-source voting systems and risk-limiting audit tools for election offices

paragraphs: VotingWorks is a nonpartisan nonprofit that builds election technology for the officials who run American elections. There are two products. VxSuite is a complete voting system designed to the latest federal standard. The organization calls it the only open-source voting system used in United States elections. Arlo is an open-source application for auditing vote tabulation after an election.

Voters mark a paper ballot by hand or with a ballot-marking device, then scan it in under three seconds. A full precinct sets up in under three minutes and the equipment folds down for transport. Arlo audits tabulation whether the ballots were counted on VxSuite or on another vendor's system, using peer-reviewed statistics. Source code and documentation are published for anyone to verify. Software integrity can be checked in the field in 30 seconds.

Jurisdictions in New Hampshire and Mississippi run real elections on the voting system. Nine states are listed as using Arlo for statewide risk-limiting audits, among them Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Texas. The work dates to 2018. It is organized as a 501c3, funded by equipment sales and support, government contracts and grants, and donations. The equipment complies with the Help America Vote Act, and HAVA grants can be used to buy it.

quote.text: Our source code and documentation are open for anyone to verify.

Poll worker records cover each worker's work history, training and performance. An asset tracking module combines tracking, chain of custody, GPS tracking of equipment, and reporting and audit history. Inventory management covers supplies during all phases of an election, before, during and after. A campaign finance module includes a public-facing portal that makes campaign finance disclosures easy to search and access. The platform is built on Microsoft Azure.

The company says more than 350 jurisdictions serving communities of all sizes use it. It was built by former election officials. Support staff are described as experts in both technical support and election knowledge. Pricing and licensing agreements are simple and do not require a long-term commitment.

paragraphs: Enhanced Voting sells an electronic ballot delivery solution for states and localities. Alongside it the company offers a public reporting product that displays election results in visual and interactive formats. A third product lets staff remake unreadable ballots with less effort and fewer mistakes. The company also supports Ballot Scout, described as vote-by-mail tracking for voters and election administrators built on USPS IMB scans.

With Enhanced Ballot, voters can access their precinct-specific ballot to mark and download it. The platform is presented as fully accessible to voters using assistive technologies like screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech input software. The company describes it as a way for military and overseas voters to securely download their specific ballots. It states that the platform conforms to federal ADA standards. The remake product ships as a cart holding a touchscreen interface, a dual camera system, label printer, barcode scanner, and a ballot printer. Enhanced Results aggregates and validates data and displays it through maps, interactive graphs, and customizable public websites.

The company says its technology is developed, maintained, and audited by election security experts. Officials quoted on the site include a former deputy elections director from the Oregon Secretary of State office. An election services director at the Virginia Department of Elections also appears among the testimonials.

paragraphs: BallotTrax tracks the status of every mail-in ballot and sends voters proactive alerts telling them where their ballot is, from printed to accepted. The company calls it a mail ballot locator and notification system. It is available in select counties, and voters can check whether their own county is eligible.

By integrating with state and county election offices, print vendors and USPS, the system knows when a ballot has been printed and mailed, returned, received and accepted for counting. Voters can choose notifications by text, email or voice alert. Election officials get tracking, reports and branding customization. Those reports are meant to help run a better election and reduce administrative costs through better forecasting and planning.

BallotTrax is a division of i3logix, Inc., based in Denver, Colorado. The site announces a second U.S. patent for its mail ballot tracking and voter notification system. It also posted that BallotTrax achieved SOC 2 compliance. Among the testimonials on the page is one attributed to the director of Multnomah County Elections in Portland.

quote.text: BallotTrax brings transparency to the voter process so you know your vote has counted.

paragraphs: Democracy Works is a nonpartisan nonprofit that builds tools meant to make it easier for voters to take part in every election. It works with election officials, major platforms, civic organizations and companies so that voters can reach accurate information.

TurboVote, the voter engagement platform, offers personalized support across the whole voting journey. Underneath it sits official election information collected, verified and published straight from state and local election offices. An Elections API delivers that enterprise-grade data across thousands of elections at every level of government. The Voting Information Project gathers voting location data directly from election officials and distributes it to voters through the Google Civic Information API. Participating jurisdictions are not charged for that program. In 2025 the organization published data for 3,462 elections across all 50 states, covering municipal, school board, county and other local contests.

The organization was founded in 2010 with the goal of making voting easier for Americans. It is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It has also partnered with platforms such as Perplexity AI and Anthropic to place reliable election information in the AI space. On the employer side, the Civic Alliance it co-founded with the CAA Foundation supports more than 1,300 member businesses.

The compliance practice files campaign finance, lobbying, pay-to-play, and Foreign Agent Registration Act reports federally, in 49 of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. That team of attorneys and paralegals is described as assisting over 230 clients with campaign finance, lobbying, and government ethics compliance. A division called Integrity sells identity and age verification products to commercial and government buyers. Overseas, the company says it has worked with candidates and political parties from Afghanistan to Ukraine and Kenya to Georgia.

Two brothers started the firm in 1983 to build what they described as the first campaign finance and reporting database. It is headquartered on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC. Compliance services are led by a former two-term Federal Election Commission chairman. The company claims that over more than 40 years almost every U.S. president has used its solutions, along with senatorial and congressional campaigns and state party initiatives from both major parties. A proprietary reporting platform gives clients real-time production and USPS tracking data. That platform also lets voters look up and track their ballot through the mail stream.
