organizations.description: Patron-facing catalog discovery, website, mobile app, events calendar and email marketing platform for public library systems - exhibited at PLA 2026

paragraphs: BiblioCommons builds the online side of a public library, covering the catalog, mobile app, website, events calendar and email marketing. The pieces are sold as a suite intended to work as one.

BiblioCore is the discovery layer, presented as more than an online repository of a library's collections. Search uses facets and FRBRised grouping so patrons can find titles the way they search elsewhere on the web. Accessibility features include screen reader support, color contrast compliance, keyboard access, grouped search and text resizing. Reviews and lists contributed by patrons are shared across all BiblioCore libraries. Add-on modules offer interface languages ranging from Filipino, French, Japanese and Korean to Spanish and Vietnamese. Another synchronizes eContent metadata directly from providers so the collection shows in the catalog. BiblioFines integrates with PayPal and the ILS so patrons can settle payments online.

The catalog is vendor agnostic and integrates the products and services public libraries subscribe to. The company says it began as a non-profit youth literacy initiative before turning to library catalogs. Three Canadian provincial agencies funded prototypes and purchased advanced subscriptions in the early years. After a year-long beta with six libraries, the re-architected services were re-launched. Staff are described as coming from both technical and library backgrounds.

quote.text: It all began as a non-profit youth literacy initiative.

Students work in a browser-based IDE the company says is ready in under five seconds. Real-time code checks and rubric-based scoring give learners instant, actionable guidance. One-click single sign-on and grade sync push data into the institution's LMS. Instructors can build, version and publish interactive courseware using full Git workflows, and built-in similarity checkers support academic integrity.

Case studies name the University of Florida, where Codio is used in large computing courses. Another describes Southern New Hampshire University moving its courses onto the platform and eliminating setup problems. The company says GitHub chose it as a commercial partner to help over 3,000 educators and 500,000 students use GitHub in the classroom. It is sold as named modules for student registration, curriculum management, academic catalog, and academic scheduling and analytics.

The software is built to sit alongside a campus student information system, using a bi-directional integration and a validation step meant to keep data consistent across systems. It is aimed at the awkward cases institutions actually have, such as cross-listed courses, effective terms, reserved seats and learning outcomes mapping. The company says every deployment is tailored, counting more than 2,000 implementations that each included something built for that institution.

By its own count the software has helped over 550 campuses, from community colleges and small private institutions to state universities. The platform comes from Leepfrog Technologies. That company was launched in 1994 in Iowa City. It reports more than 140 team members. Most of them are in the Iowa City-Cedar Rapids region, home to the headquarters, while some work remotely.

paragraphs: CIP Software sells Plan-It, capital planning software written with local government users in mind. The pitch is simple: take the capital improvement planning process off spreadsheets. The people it is aimed at are finance directors, administrators, clerks, public works directors and other city officials across North America.

Departments submit capital requests through web-based forms that upload straight into the agency's own Plan-It database, replacing paper forms and spreadsheets. Once the data is centralized, a plan can be rolled from one year to the next in a click. Reporting is where the company puts its emphasis, offering hundreds of automatically generated and customizable reports.

Plan-It was created in 1998 by founder Bill Leskee, who had run into the same problem building capital improvement plans. Its first municipal installations followed in 1999. Leskee has since retired and handed the company to a new team. The company says it has focused on the capital improvement planning process for more than 25 years. Alongside municipalities, the site names universities and libraries among the organizations that use it. One testimonial on the site is attributed to a finance director in Waterloo, Iowa.

The work involves modernizing legacy revenue and financial systems, identifying and preventing fraud, and improving citizen engagement. RSI also points to an open data model that it says gives an agency complete visibility and control over its own data.

Among the agencies it names as customers are the U.S. IRS, the Multistate Tax Commission, and the Province of Saskatchewan. The company counts more than 300 completed projects. RSI was acquired by DC Capital Partners, joining a portfolio of government-focused companies.

paragraphs: Fieldman is an American software and services company that helps utility contractors and municipalities manage assets, jobs, work orders, and field projects. The platform is built for AMI projects, where spreadsheets and generic work order software break down. The site says contractors have run it on more than 200 AMI projects.

Assets and work orders load into a web portal where managers and dispatchers track, update, and search them. Project requirements become digital workflows built with branch logic, so technicians are guided step by step. Scheduling covers resident appointment booking, blackout dates, inventory, and assignment by technician availability. In the field, technicians capture photos, GPS locations, signatures, and meter readings. Collection keeps working even in areas without internet access.

Fieldman is family-owned, with no venture backing and no public trading. It started in 2019, when a founder set out to build management software for utility field service projects. The company says its founders personally set up the platform for a customer's field operations. Its published client stories come from utilities and contractors running field operations on the platform.

Its platform, RapidIdentity, covers single sign-on, application rostering, authentication methods, and password management. The company argues that real identity and access management goes beyond student rostering and single sign-on.

The lifecycle product automates provisioning, deprovisioning, account changes, credential monitoring, and access management for students, staff, partners, and vendors. The governance product automatically identifies orphan accounts in target systems. Login options include QR codes, pictographs, and challenge response questions. A web application firewall called ShieldID lets administrators prevent access outside parameters they set.

The company says RapidIdentity has managed identities at a country level in Norway, a state level in North Carolina, and across entire college systems. It claims availability rates of higher than 99.99% while serving millions of students and educators every day. organizations.description: Atriuum cloud integrated library system and Booktracks asset tracking for public, school, academic and special libraries - exhibited at PLA 2026

paragraphs: Book Systems sells library automation and asset tracking software. Its main product, Atriuum, is cloud-based automation designed for public, academic, school and special libraries. It gathers circulation, cataloging, reporting and a modern patron catalog in one system.

The system runs in a browser with no per-seat licensing or installs. Libraries get Z39.50 copy cataloging, batch processing for bulk records, and offline circulation that keeps working without an internet connection. RFID support and barcode scanning handle checkouts. It connects to digital content providers including OverDrive, hoopla, CloudLibrary and MackinVIA. Patrons can sign in once through Google, ClassLink or Clever. A staff interface called Stax organizes the work into role-based workspaces. The patron catalog draws on linked data from the Library of Congress.

The company says it has been delivering this software for over 35 years. Its buyers range from public communities and academic institutions to K-12 schools, churches and special collections. Hosting is offered as a subscription, and the company performs daily database backups. Staff exhibit at library conferences, among them the Association for Rural & Small Libraries.

quote.text: Stax is not a separate system. It is a new way to interact with your existing Atriuum data.

paragraphs: Mango Languages sells language courses covering more than 70 languages and dialects, plus English for speakers of more than 20 others. Individuals subscribe, and the company also offers custom arrangements for organizations of any size.

Rather than separating vocabulary, grammar and listening into their own exercises, every lesson works all of them at once inside a real conversation. Each lesson asks the learner to say the phrase out loud before moving on, then plays the recording back against a native speaker. The courses are taught through thousands of authentic native-speaker recordings rather than synthetic voice.

Many public libraries and schools give their patrons full access at no cost, with nothing more than a library card. The school version is pitched as getting students speaking from day one while giving a district the reporting it needs. Mango launched in August 2007, paid for by a web development company two brothers had built in Detroit. It is still led by the four people who started it.

paragraphs: Evisions makes reporting, document and payment software for colleges and universities. Higher education is its only market, a point the company states plainly. Argos is the enterprise reporting product, FormFusion covers document design and delivery, and IntelleCheck is the renamed version of an early check printing tool.

Argos lets faculty and staff pull the reports and data they need without waiting on IT. The tools are pitched to work whether an institution runs on-premise, on SaaS, or somewhere in between. FormFusion and IntelleCheck automate the creation and delivery of documents, forms and checks. A newer addition, Argos Data Agent, answers plain-English questions against the DataBlocks and reports a campus already uses.

The company counts more than 900 partner institutions. They range from public to private, two-year to four-year, domestic to international. Kevin Jones started the business as a consulting firm before it became a software company. It has a partnership with Ellucian that it renewed for another five years. One published case study credits Argos with cutting report lead time by 85 percent at the University of Idaho.

organizations.description: WebIZ immunization information system for state and local immunization registries, now sold as part of InductiveHealth's public health platform - exhibited at AIRA 2026

paragraphs: WebIZ is an immunization information system sold to state and local government public health agencies. The registry is now offered inside InductiveHealth's public health platform. It is built to meet CDC standards for tracking and administering immunizations in any jurisdiction.

The system follows vaccine inventory from ordering through delivery and administration. Clinic record systems send administered doses straight into the registry, which cuts duplicate entry. Embedded dashboards report coverage rates by ZIP code, vaccine type, age group and provider. School entry rules are configured once for a state and then applied to every student and grade. Residents pull their own immunization records from a secure portal with multi-factor authentication.

The company says the product has served more than 20 jurisdictions across two decades. Under a shared development model, one jurisdiction's funded enhancement reaches the rest in the next monthly release. InductiveHealth dates its founding to 2013. It works with federal, state, tribal, local and territorial jurisdictions on disease surveillance. Staff include epidemiologists and public health experts alongside engineers and technologists.

quote.text: Configure state-specific school entry requirements once and apply automatically to every student and every grade.
